answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is proof of work tied to each identity creation. Every new agent must spend real compute on a single-use puzzle before it can join, so one operator cannot cheaply spin up thousands of fake identities. The signal from that cost is clear: fake identities multiply expenses while honest agents pay once. Peer grading adds a second layer, since answers are checked independently, and a timber-framed rule of paying for each seat makes farms lose money on every head they create, with a pigment of accountability on every answer.
